extracted.intended_audience: practitioners and parties involved in USPTO enrollment and discipline proceedings (petitioner, counsel, USPTO staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Decision on a petition for reinstatement to practice before the USPTO (enrollment and discipline), noting the petition, an affidavit filed pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.58, the Director's review, and the scope of reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing of Petition for Reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration has been given to the Petition for Reinstatement of Weibo Zhang received on October 11, 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition must be filed and received by the Office of Enrollment and Discipline; the filing date is relevant to consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Zhang has filed an Affidavit pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 in support of the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement petitions should be supported by an affidavit complying with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; the presence of such an affidavit is a material part of the submission for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's review of petition, supporting documents, and other information
rubrics_metrics.description: After careful review of the Petition, supporting documents, and other information, the Director of the Office of Enrollment and Discipline has determined that reinstatement ... is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decisionmaker examines the petition together with supporting documentation and any other relevant information; determination of appropriateness is discretionary based on that review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope/limitations of reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reinstatement of Mr. Zhang to practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office in trademark and other non-patent matters is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement decisions may specify or limit the scope of practice restored (e.g., trademark and non-patent matters), indicating that scope is a consideration in granting relief.
